chunks: My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa said, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abu Najran, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim, on the authority of Habib al-Sajistani, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (AS) who said:

Verily, it is stated in the Torah: O Musa! Verily, I have created you, chosen you, strengthened you, commanded you for My Obedience, and prohibited you from disobeying Me. Therefore, if you obey Me I will help you to obey Me and if you disobey Me, I will not help you to disobey me. O Musa! I have favored you in your obedience to Me, and I have evidence over you in your disobedience of Me.
ai.seo_question: What does the Torah say about God's relationship with Musa regarding obedience and disobedience?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration from the Torah to demonstrate the continuity of divine principles across scriptures, specifically highlighting the concept of 'Tawfiq' (divine assistance) for the obedient and the establishment of 'Hujjah' (divine proof) against the disobedient. This reinforces the Shia theological view that God’s help is not automatic but contingent upon human agency and faithfulness, a theme central to the chapter on Command and Prohibition.
